mintAuthority.summary: The 13 issuer-native MIM deployments expose owner-controlled mint functions. Ethereum's owner is a 5/11 Safe with no modules or guard detected; the other 12 native owner Safes are enumerated with verified thresholds and empty module reads, while their guard status remains unverified. The Berachain LayerZero OFT representation is excluded from Mint Authority and remains in Bridge Risk.

mintIncidents.summary: Abracadabra cauldron borrow logic was exploited to enable unauthorized MIM borrowing, turning the stablecoin mint/borrow route into bad debt.

Flawed collateral accounting in Abracadabra's GMX-integrated gmCauldrons left phantom collateral after failed deposit orders and self-liquidation, letting the attacker borrow about 13.4M MIM (~$13M in ETH) against collateral the system failed to remove.

A cook() action-sequencing flaw in deprecated CauldronV4 contracts reset the solvency-check flag, letting attackers borrow about 1.79M MIM with no collateral; the DAO bought back the supply to defend the peg.

review.evidence: Ethereum MIM owner reads and Sourcify ABI identify a 5/11 Safe owner with direct owner-controlled mint functions on the token. Re-verified by direct chain reads at Ethereum block 25575152 on 2026-07-20: MIM 0x99d8a9c45b2eca8864373a26d1459e3dff1e17f3 owner() returns Safe 0x5f0DeE98360d8200b20812e174d139A1a633EDd2, which returns getThreshold()=5 over the same eleven owners, an empty getModulesPaginated array, a zero guard slot, and Safe 1.3.0 masterCopy 0xd9db270c1b5e3bd161e8c8503c55ceabee709552. Economic-control adjudication: the token owner Safe holds unconditional mint and mintToBentoBox entry points with no on-chain cap, no timelock, and no independent bound, so the mint cap is economically unbounded. There is no supply-versus-reserve attestation of any cadence and the token-level owner mint means outstanding MIM cannot be reconciled to cauldron collateral from on-chain reads alone, so reconciliation stays unknown, and no financial regulator supervises Abracadabra. 2026-07-21 follow-up closes the two prior open questions: (1) the verified MagicInternetMoneyV1.sol source shows both mint() and mintToBentoBox() are onlyOwner with no separate cauldron-level minter role, cauldrons draw down MIM the owner has pre-minted into BentoBox rather than minting directly themselves, and mint() itself enforces a soft per-period rate limiter (MINTING_INCREASE=15000/1e5=15% growth of totalSupply per rolling 24-hour MINTING_PERIOD), though the owner can still call mint repeatedly with no absolute ceiling, so the cap remains economically unbounded despite this rate-of-growth throttle; (2) the 13 issuer-native MIM deployments are now enumerated in controls with chain-specific owner Safes, while the Berachain LayerZero OFT representation is excluded from Mint Authority and remains in bridgeRouteRisk. The non-Ethereum Safe proxy guard getters reverted, so their guard state remains unverified rather than inferred. Economic-posture fields reviewed 2026-08-15: the existing unbounded, unknown-reconciliation, and no-supervision verdicts remain supported by the owner-mint and attestation evidence. Wave 2 external review 2026-08-15: Abracadabra's token, cauldron, deployment, and analytics pages expose supply and collateral data but no recurring independent report reconciles all MIM liabilities, including owner-level minting across deployments.
